```{r setup}
library(tiltedTMLE)
```

## Overview

`tiltedTMLE` estimates tilted average treatment effect (ATE) estimands of
the form

\deqn{\tau_h = \frac{E[h(X)(Q(X,1)-Q(X,0))]}{E[h(X)]}}

for a tilting function `h(x)` that is either fixed and known, or itself a
function of an estimated nuisance that must be targeted alongside the
outcome regression. There are three entry points, one per setting:

- `estimate_tau_h_fixed()` -- `h(x)` is a fixed, precomputed weight (e.g.
  `h(x) = 1` for the plain ATE), estimated with a single TMLE targeting
  step.
- `estimate_tau_h_internal_tilted()` -- `h(x) = eta(g(x))`, a known
  function of the treatment propensity score, within one study
  population (ATE/ATT/ATC/ATO). `g` is iteratively targeted.
- `estimate_tau_h_external_tilted()` -- `h(x) = eta(s(x))`, a known
  function of the selection propensity score between an internal trial
  and an external covariate-only population (ATE-I/ATE-E/ATE-O). The
  selection score `s` is iteratively targeted.

The full derivations, efficient influence functions, and algorithm
pseudocode are in `TMLE_tilted_algorithms.pdf` at the package source
root -- this vignette only covers how to call the three entry points.

## A simulated internal trial, plus external covariates

```{r sim-data}
set.seed(42)
n <- 300 # internal trial
m <- 300 # external, covariate-only

W1 <- rnorm(n + m)
W2 <- rnorm(n + m)
D <- c(rep(1L, n), rep(0L, m)) # 1 = internal trial, 0 = external
Ws <- data.frame(X1 = W1, X2 = W2)

A <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.3 * W1[1:n] - 0.2 * W2[1:n]))
Y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.3 + 0.5 * A + 0.3 * W1[1:n] - 0.2 * W2[1:n]))
W <- Ws[1:n, , drop = FALSE] # internal-only covariates
```

## Fixed h: the plain ATE

```{r fixed-ate}
out_ate <- estimate_tau_h_fixed(Y, A, W, h = rep(1, n), n_boot = 50)
out_ate$TMLE
out_ate$TMLE_CI
```

## Internally tilted: the ATT

`h(x) = eta(g(x)) = g(x)` tilts the ATE toward the treated population.
`tilt_spec()` supplies `eta`/`eta_dot` for the four named internal
estimands (`"ATE"`, `"ATT"`, `"ATC"`, `"ATO"`).

```{r internal-att}
spec_att <- tilt_spec("ATT")
out_att <- estimate_tau_h_internal_tilted(Y, A, W, spec_att$eta, spec_att$eta_dot)
out_att$TMLE
out_att$TMLE_iter
```

## Externally tilted: the overlap population (ATE-O)

`h(x) = eta(s(x)) = 1 - s(x)` tilts toward covariate overlap between the
internal trial and the external population. This needs the full pooled
data: `Y`/`A` observed only on the internal rows, `D` and `Ws` for all
`n + m` rows. `tilt_spec_external()` supplies `eta`/`eta_dot` for the
three named external estimands (`"ATE-I"`, `"ATE-E"`, `"ATE-O"`).

```{r external-ateo}
spec_o <- tilt_spec_external("ATE-O")
out_ateo <- estimate_tau_h_external_tilted(Y, A, D, Ws, spec_o$eta, spec_o$eta_dot)
out_ateo$TMLE
out_ateo$TMLE_iter
```

## Reading the output

All three entry points return a list including `TMLE` (point estimate),
`TMLE_se`/`TMLE_CI` (EIF-based Wald inference), plus un-targeted
benchmark estimators (`MLE`, `IPW`, and `AIPW` where defined) and the
underlying fitted-nuisance objects (`Qfit`, `gfit`, and `sfit` for the
externally tilted case) for further inspection. See `?estimate_tau_h_fixed`,
`?estimate_tau_h_internal_tilted`, and `?estimate_tau_h_external_tilted`
for the full set of arguments (SuperLearner nuisance fitting, propensity
truncation bounds, bootstrap options).
